name: ABB India Ltd.
business_summary: Indian arm (75% owned by ABB Ltd, Switzerland) of the global electrification and automation group: electrification (low/medium-voltage switchgear, breakers, drives, building products), motion (motors, drives, traction), process automation (control systems, measurement, service) and, until its sale in early 2026, robotics and discrete automation (the Mar-2026 quarter PAT of Rs 1,784 cr includes an exceptional gain on selling the robotics business). Calendar-year reporter: Q2 CY26 revenue Rs 3,559 cr (+21%), EBITDA margin 13%, order backlog ~Rs 11,900 cr. Debt-free with large cash; about 13% of revenue exports; trades at ~91x trailing earnings and 15x book. Promoters at the 75% maximum, so no further promoter sell-down is possible without breaching minimum public shareholding.

exposures.mechanism: Data-centre electrification (switchgear, drives, UPS/DC distribution, automation) is a named growth vertical; ABB Ltd launched a DC portfolio for AI data centres (2026-09-21). Assume data centres ~8% of India revenue today. Theme +1 SSU = doubling of India DC build intensity -> +8% revenue at ~28% contribution -> EBITDA +16%; x0.97 EV/MCap x persistence 0.5 (structural) discounted for share/competition risk = +3.0 (wide). Order intake +50% in Q2 CY26 but ~30pp below group growth because DC orders are booked by the parent.

evidence.note: India order inflows +50% in Q2 vs +81% for global ABB; gap partly due to orders booked by parent
AI and data-centre boom created a Rs 12,000 cr revenue pipeline for the automation stock

exposures.mechanism: Electrification products (breakers, switchgear, low/medium voltage drives) feed grid, renewables, metro/rail and buildings; ~35% of revenue. +1 SSU (a step-up in grid/transmission capex intensity) -> +6% revenue at 30% contribution vs 14% margin -> EBITDA +13%; x0.97 x0.5 x discount for competition (Siemens, Hitachi, CG Power, Schneider) = +2.5. Backlog Rs 11,900 cr (0.85x revenue) is lower visibility than CG Power (1.37x).

evidence.note: Backlog ~Rs 11,900 cr (0.85x annualised revenue), ~40% to complete in two quarters

exposures.mechanism: Motion/drives, process automation and machine-building customers (~55% of revenue) track private capex. +10pp private capex growth -> +4% revenue (lagged) at ~28% contribution vs 14% margin -> EBITDA +8%; x0.97 x persistence 0.5 = +3.9, trimmed to +3.5. Q2 CY26 revenue +21% to Rs 3,559 cr, first-half revenue Rs 6,743 cr; CFO sees volume-led growth.

evidence.note: Highest ever Q2 revenue Rs 3,559 cr; growth to be volume-led; margin recovery to take time

exposures.mechanism: Utilities, railways/metro, water and public infrastructure ~25% of revenue. +10% government capex growth -> +2.5% revenue -> EBITDA +5%; x0.97 x0.3 = +1.5.

evidence.note: No direct disclosure fetched; model estimate

exposures.mechanism: Sentiment/valuation channel from global ABB: on 2026-10-20 ABB Ltd fell on 'AI worries' despite record orders; ABB India fell 6% on 2026-10-21 (worst day in five months) and 12% in five days (Goodreturns). At P/E 91x, a +10% change in AI capex expectations moves the multiple ~1-2% plus orders; w = +1.2. Overlaps T_DATA_CENTRES_IN; Director should net.

evidence.note: ABB India fell as much as 6% on parent's business update; 14 of 33 analysts have Sell
Shares fell >12% in five days; brokerages cautious

exposures.mechanism: ABB India imports a large share of components and finished products from the group (USD/EUR/CHF), ~30% of sales; exports ~13% of revenue (down from 17%). Net exposure ~17% of sales; +3% INR weakness -> +0.5% of sales -> EBITDA -3.6% pre; ~50% hedged/passed -> -1.8%; x0.97 x0.35 = -0.6, rounded -0.8. CFO named forex volatility and commodities as the margin drag. Pack empirical +1.63 per +3% (t +0.9) has the opposite sign and is insignificant.

evidence.note: Margin pressure from commodities and forex volatility; recovery depends on volatility settling

exposures.mechanism: Copper (cables, windings, busbars, motors) ~6% of sales. +10% -> 0.6% of sales -> EBITDA -4.3% pre; ~55% recovered through price-variation clauses and list-price rises -> -1.9%; x0.97 x0.35 = -0.65. Pack empirical copper is POSITIVE (+1.69 per +10%, t +1.9) because copper strength proxies the global electrification/capex upcycle; the structural cost edge is therefore shrunk to -0.4 with a range crossing zero. Copper is -2.4% since June.

evidence.note: Empirical copper +1.69 (t +1.9): sign conflict with cost channel

exposures.mechanism: Steel (enclosures, structures, motors) ~5% of sales. +7% -> 0.35% of sales -> -2.5% EBITDA pre; 50% recovered; x0.97 x0.35 = -0.4.

evidence.note: Material costs cited as main margin pressure

exposures.mechanism: Pack empirical +1.68 per +10% Brent (t +2.5): higher crude lifts oil-and-gas, refining and petrochemical capex (process automation and drives), and correlates with the commodity/capex upcycle; offset by general cost and rate pressure. Kept at +0.6 (about one third of empirical). Low confidence because the same regime also coincides with ABB India's strong stock in 2025-26.

Debt-free with Rs 1,799 cr other income (large cash), so direct cost of debt is nil; sensitivity is valuation: P/E 91x, 15x book -> equity duration ~25 years. +25bp in the discount rate -> ~-1.0% value, plus weaker private capex sentiment -0.2. RBI hiked to 5.50% on 2026-10-07.

Manufacturing relocation to India lifts demand for automation and electrification (factories, EMS, batteries, semiconductors). +1 SSU -> +2% medium-term revenue at 28% contribution -> EBITDA +4% x0.97 x0.5 x0.5 = +1.0. Risk: the ABB-Mitsubishi Electric JV (Asia-Pacific) is seen as an export overhang (InCred).

evidence.note: InCred: new ABB-Mitsubishi JV could overhang ABB India exports to Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia

supply_chain.note: 75% promoter; group supplies imported products; some orders booked at parent level (India order growth +50% vs group +81% in Q2 CY26)
motors, drives, switchgear; faster growth, bigger backlog (1.37x vs 0.85x)

current_state.trend: Q2 CY26: revenue Rs 3,559 cr (+21%, record Q2), EBITDA Rs 447 cr (+11.4%, margin 13% vs 14%), PAT Rs 362 cr (+3%), order inflow +50% (group +81%), backlog ~Rs 11,900 cr. CFO: growth volume-led, margin recovery will take time due to commodities and forex. Mar-2026 quarter PAT Rs 1,784 cr was inflated by an exceptional gain from selling the robotics business; continuing-operations PAT was Rs 342 cr (-25%).
